paragraphs: Rav Shmuel bar Sasartai—in Bava Kamma 102b, Sasarti—went to Rome. The queen lost an ornament, and the king proclaimed that whoever returned it within thirty days would receive such-and-such, but if after thirty days, he would be put to death. He returned it after thirty days and explained that had he returned it within thirty days, it would have appeared that he returned it from fear of the king; now, however, he returned it from dread of the Lord of Hosts and the splendor of His majesty. The king said, “Blessed is the Lord, the God of Shmuel”; he sanctified the Name. Jerusalem Bava Metzia, chapter 2, halakhah 5. Ta'anit 14a: “What was the conclusion?” R' Shmuel bar Sasartai gave the answer. Rav Hiyya bar Ashi also reported it in Rav's name. In R' Avahu's name: Jerusalem Ha-Zahav, halakhah 2; and the beginning of Arba Mitot.
